Params: As the aircraft tears through the clouds, you glance down.
The wild sea wind has ripped the clouds into thin, curling wisps. Through their sheer veil, a tired gray-blue stretches endlessly below, an ocean that mirrors the sky above.
And across that vast blue, a thin line of blood-red sears the distance like a scar burned into crystal.
The frame pod rests on its shock-dampening mount. As you lean in, the data on its display slowly fades.
Through the viewport, Karenina's frame materializes, and a faint tremor from the internal climate system hums against your palm, steady as breathing.
You remember that figure slumped over the desk in the lounge. Her hair was a wild, tangled mess, and structural blueprints were scattered across every surface of the room.
So this is the finished product.
Commandant, I'll go over the data one last time...
I've been handling the squad's frame upkeep. This is more my territory. I'll leave Commandant's gear check to you.
The craft angles downward, tilting just enough for the sea below to come into focus. A Construct's vision pulls every surging crest into vivid relief.
Below, a savage engagement tears through the water, gunfire kicking up crimson walls of foam.
The whales' spines drift in and out of the red-tinged haze, mountain after mountain of bone and flesh closing off the Vega's route. Suppression fire alone keeps them from surging forward.
On the Balder's deck, Karenina presses a hand hard against her temple, her M.I.N.D. seething. Every word costs her more processing power than it should, dragged out through the pain.
Keep up... suppressive fire. Don't let them... push any closer to... Balder... ngh...
Captain, let us handle this... There are other Constructs on board, you don't have to—
(Dammit... what the hell is going on with my... my M.I.N.D...)
Emergency frame switch protocol initiated.\nETA: 2 minutes. A dispatched commandant will assume M.I.N.D. stabilization duties.
Emergency frame switch protocol initiated. ETA: 2 minutes. A dispatched commandant will assume M.I.N.D. stabilization duties.
Her frame has been ready for a long time; every adaptation test passed cleanly. But her M.I.N.D. at this moment is a storm of noise, as unreadable as primordial chaos.
My M.I.N.D. is in no shape to—
Her voice catches in her throat.
Everything in her field of vision shudders and heaves.
Then a familiar Mind Beacon lights up inside her M.I.N.D., like the first navigation light blazing across a black sea, anchoring every sense of direction she'd lost.
The agony has pushed her M.I.N.D. to the edge of breaking. Now a quiet, gentle force folds around it, lifting the broken pieces as carefully as if they were made of cloud.
Once the connection locks into place, her M.I.N.D. at last begins to stabilize. The shattered edges draw together, healing inch by slow inch.
Frame pre-activation sequence underway. Estimated completion: 5 minutes.
Frame pre-activation sequence underway. Estimated completion: 5 minutes.
...It's nothing. Just some minor hiccups. Nothing I can't deal with myself.
She sounds like herself again at last.
But you...! Why didn't you... why didn't you give me a heads-up?!
I thought with us on separate missions, you were gonna miss my new frame completely...
Hold on. If you're the one handling the delivery...
That means... while I was NOT THERE...
You already saw my new frame that I spent FOREVER designing?!
The Construct girl's face rounds into a puffed-up scowl.
Uh oh. Uh oh uh oh...
I have a really bad feeling about where this is going...
Across the M.I.N.D. connection, a flustered data stream contorts itself into something resembling a pretzel.
Is there a problem?! That was supposed to be another first meeting! Between this version of me and you!
Wait. No. That's not what I... It's the reaction! The praise! Who's gonna give me back my moment?!
Boss... it's Gray Raven's mission. Lee being here kind of tracks... M-maybe try taking a breath first...
What do you know, you idiot! This is a brand new frame we're talking—
Karenina, parameter calibration's finished. You're clear for the switch once pre-activation wraps up.
The moment that familiar voice sounds, Karenina's face goes completely still.
WHA—?! Lucia?! Why are you here too?!
This is Gray Raven's mission. So here I am.
You know, sometimes the secret to world peace is really simple. Everyone just shuts up.
But hey, look on the bright side. Stacking a few rage buffs before a fight? That's just free stats.
Karenina, your new frame looks great.
You did an amazing job with the design.
I-I... it's not like I was fishing for compliments or anything...
Every prickly edge of her mood dissolves at once.
Sometimes the secret to world peace is really simple. Just keep talking.
Frame pre-activation sequence complete. Transport pod has successfully entered the atmosphere.
Frame pre-activation sequence complete. Transport pod has successfully entered the atmosphere.
Severing sensory input. Entering short-term hibernation. Estimated duration: 67 seconds.
Severing sensory input. Entering short-term hibernation. Estimated duration: 67 seconds.
Skip it. My adaptation data's been stable the whole time, and I'm already fully matched with this frame.
I can stay conscious through the whole process. It'll be faster.
>>>> Commencing frame switch authorization, please enter the activation parameter.
>>>> Please refrain from interrupting the connection during consciousness transfer.
Inside the pod, the frame's eyes slide open, still cold with mechanical emptiness. But you know the flame of a soul will catch soon, and those eyes will burn with life.
Your group gathers to lift Karenina from the pod.
The cabin's sterile air rushes into her lungs, and her lips part, just barely, trembling with the first breath of renewed life.

Frigid wind pours through the aircraft's open hatch. The frame's hands rest in yours, and the metal coldness is already fading. Now that the soul inside has awakened, living warmth will soon flood back into this body, indistinguishable from flesh and blood.
The frame cocks her head at you.
Through the M.I.N.D. connection, you feel a bright spark, prickly and scorching, hurtling upward along a towering beam of light like a wildfire racing up an ancient tree.
Before you, the frame's eyes stir with life. The girl named Karenina is waking up inside this body.
See you in a bit, Karenina.
She presses her cap down against the gust and turns, the cloud sea stretching vast and restless at her back. The battlefield waits just beyond.
See you in a bit, Commandant.
She spins through the air like a wheeling bird, swallowed by the vastness of the sky, light pouring over her.
The frame, barely awake, is already in freefall toward the whales.
Lucia, Lee, get ready for cover fire and support.
Inside the Balder's dock bay, her old frame's senses wash away like color unfurling in the water. For one fleeting instant, Karenina feels certain that if she glances back, 【kuroname】 will be there.
She is going to experience the entire frame transfer fully conscious, not missing a single second.

An emptiness without origin surrounds her. But deep in her consciousness, a beacon holds firm, and she does not lose her way. She rises, climbing through the vast ocean and the endless sky, back toward the place she belongs.
Rebirth begins with the body. Sensation floods her limbs, and instinct follows. A hatchling spreading its wings, she reaches out, trying to touch something warm.

Then comes breath. The high, cold air cuts into her lungs. The vital fluid on her tongue tastes of life. That person's warmth lingers on her skin, and her own body rises to meet it, heat kindling like an answer.

Then comes sound. That voice lights the spark deep inside her. Great trees surge skyward, waves roar forward, and her single speck of starlight catches, blazing into a wildfire that swallows the heavens.
Finally, light arrives. In the very first instant of her becoming, a gaze finds her. The commandant's eyes are on her.
(Phew... See you in a bit, Commandant.)
She cuts through the howling wind and weightlessness, her new frame answering to her will.
Below her, the sea stretches wide, her first battlefield.
Gray Raven, this is Captain Karenina, Engineering Force. Requesting tactical support. Wipe out the whale pod and secure the Vega.
She keeps her voice brisk and official, trying to smother the obvious glee that keeps slipping through.
Just off her flank, a dark figure keeps pace.
Lee offers a brief nod, then extends his frame. The temporary boosters detach, and he angles his body to fix his descent point before shooting toward the sea like an arrow loosed from its string.
In that instant of crossing paths, another silhouette flashes through her vision.
Captain Karenina. Gray Raven will provide cover and help you take them down.
Karenina catches Lucia's calm gaze and hesitates, just briefly. Then the generous ship captain returns it with a look of affirmation.
Not every day we get to fight together. Try not to slow me down!
The great anchor hits the water a beat before Karenina, blooming into a surfboard that catches her smoothly atop the swell.
She cuts hard before a churning wall of water, her thrusters blasting a shock of air as she veers straight toward the largest of the whales.
I'll take the big ones out here. You two get on the Vega and get everyone out.
Right behind her, Lucia and Lee carve twin trails through the blood-red waves, their surfboards angled toward the whale-surrounded Vega.
Fire pours from the Balder's guns onto the twisted Red Tide creatures. As Gray Raven and Karenina join the battle, the momentum on the water shifts decisively.
Alright. Time for some percussive maintenance.

A little over ten minutes pass. Karenina slams her anchor deep into the skull of the final whale. The bone and sinew cave inward, and a geyser of blood-red fluid erupts from the wreckage. Expressionless, she sidesteps the spray and rips the anchor loose.
Karenina nudges her cap back into place, the faintest curve lifting her lips. She glances over at the Vega.
There, Mara leans against the rail, her anxious gaze still locked on the young captain. She has been watching the whole time.
Lee stands on the Vega's deck, a slight frown settling on his face.
These things rode in with the Red Tide, but they don't match any known Hetero-Creature patterns.
New Ascendant creations? They didn't hit nearly as hard as the ones on land.
...Let's hope there isn't something worse lurking behind them.
Commandant, we're wrapping things up here. Did you make it onto the Balder alright?
One by one, the whales slip beneath the surface, red foam thrashing into the vast gray-blue waters.
The ocean takes the crimson in, yet it does not dissolve. It lingers, undigested.
Karenina's brow knots as she stares at the blood-red stain. The waves thin it out, but it does not vanish. She spins her board and angles away.
A whale call erupts without warning.
The humpback she has just felled, the one that should be sinking into the abyss, raises its skull instead.
Red ichor weeps from the voids where its eyes once were, slithering down the fissured flesh. The mouth gapes open, and a long, resonant cry of pure sorrow spills forth.
It does not travel through air or sea. The sound reverberates straight into Karenina's M.I.N.D., and the pain surges back with it, threatening to consume her consciousness whole.
Wind rushes by her, and then, without warning, the air loses its bloody, briny tang.
A strange sensation wriggles through her M.I.N.D.
Karenina locks up and runs an immediate check on her sensory input and data acquisition modules.
The diagnostic flags nothing. But even as the values hold steady, the world before her eyes is graying out, color draining fast. Her vision is going.
Light's warmth drains away. The wind's flow thins to nothing. Even the pain grows distant. The only sensation left is a cold, clenching pressure that grips her "heart."

She is being stripped, layer by layer, and locked inside a glass cage. Amid the rising tide of whale calls, the commandant's Mind Beacon pulses. It's so close she could almost touch it, yet impossibly far, as if it belongs to another world.
She does not answer. She cannot answer.
The Drift Anchor's equilibrium system lurches, as if thrown off balance by an uninvited creature that has stepped onto the board.
She drags in a sharp breath, and the nearly extinguished ember inside her detonates, roaring back to life. In that single heartbeat, Karenina reclaims her breath.

Real wind slams into her lungs. The taste of vital fluid seeps from a wound inside her mouth, which she does not remember biting open, and the steady, unrelenting pain anchors her. She is still here. Her mind is still her own.
Are you alright? Get back first.
Something's wrong with your frame. Come back first.
I'm fine... On my way back.
The thruster blasts a white skirt of foam across the water. A small mechanical claw hooks silently onto the surfboard's edge, then disappears in the next surge of rolling waves.
Salt water sheets across the dock bay as Karenina skids in on the surfboard. She's still fighting for her footing when her eyes land on you, the person she hasn't seen in a         "long" while.

Her gaze drifts past your shoulder. A cavernous emptiness fills the dock bay, broken only by the two new faces from her cable-laying crew and Larsen, the marine engineer sent by the Transatlantic Economic Community.
Where are Lucia and Lee? They should've gotten back before me.
Still fighting out there. Are you okay?
Please, I can handle myself... Check on the Vega first.
The boat sent for the Vega has not come back. Karenina's golden eyes carry a subtle edge of worry until Lucia's voice finally cuts through the comms channel.
Commandant, one crew member on the Vega is badly hurt. The rest have minor injuries, nothing serious... But they're refusing to head back for repairs.
Refusing repairs? I get that time's tight, but they're not the only ship heading to the southern node... No, you know what, let me talk to them. Lucia, put Mara on!
She keys into the comms without hesitation. Soon after, Mara's warm, familiar tone sounds through the terminal.
Mara, the threat's cleared. You can head back and get patched up...
That won't be necessary, Karenina. We need to keep moving toward the southern node. There isn't time to spare.
But your cable layer got torn up in that fight, didn't it...
Karenina's words are still half-formed when Mara interrupts, her tone soft but leaving no room for debate.
Captain Karenina, we're engineers. Fixing things is our job, isn't it?
If something goes wrong down the line, your ship might not even make it back. I mean...
The words trail off, and a mutual silence falls over both ends of the channel.
Child, we both know these cable layers were never designed with a return trip in mind. There's only one vessel out here that can cross the Red Tide. The Balder.
Most of the anti-Punishing Virus systems on these ships are barely prototypes. No guarantee how long they'll hold. Whether we make it back... that's not something we can afford to dwell on.
Then at least run one more check first. Exhaust every option you've got. You're an engineer. You know that inspections...
That gentle tone reaches her like fingertips brushing lightly across her forehead.

I've lived through the good days... Back when everyone believed there wasn't a hurdle we couldn't clear, no problem too tangled to work out. Life kept moving forward, and hard work paid off. It felt like things would only ever get better.
Through the comm, the girl's quiet breathing whispers against her ear. Mara shuts her eyes and listens, imagining how Karenina grew, step by step, into the person on the other end of the line.
But she herself is old now. Worn thin, and a little weary of the world.
I don't know what's coming. I don't know if I'll make it. What I do know is I'm sick of waiting in place.

Time has walked a long road through me. Long enough for the whole world to turn itself inside out. And all I could do, year after year, was say goodbye. My mentors. My colleagues. My students. Then sit in an empty office and wait for their obituaries to show up.
It's not about winning. It's not about hope. I just... I need to do something. That's all.
Listen to me. Still sounds a little noble, doesn't it? But truth is, I really can't stand those noble people...
Whatever you can't handle, I'll pick up the slack. Everyone here can do something. You're not facing this by yourself—
Then just tell yourself I got tired. That I wanted to run away...
Away from a world gone barren, where I've got nothing left to give.
Her voice sounds as gentle as ever.
That's not true! Someone who wanted to run would never make a choice like this... You're the one who said it, remember? This is like an exciting adventure.
...I did say that. And my heart's racing like I'm young again, all because of this adventure.
I wanted to leave you with a good impression. I didn't want to make you unhappy. Not again.
Karenina... I was part of your Construct modification experiment.
The warmth drains from her voice.
You were what Dr. Kalon left behind. I had to save you. Or maybe... saving you was the only way I could save myself back then.
I heard you were not very happy afterward. "Not very happy"... I'm making it sound so small, aren't I?
I'm sorry. For everything we did without ever asking how you felt... Looking back now, I think that was the first time I ran away. Right in front of young Wise, too...
Karenina dips her head just enough for the cap brim to shadow her eyes. Across the rolling, sea-deep swell of years, she glances back at the person she once was.
Really? I don't remember any of that... You old folks seriously overthink everything.
I never blamed you. And I don't hate you.
I'm all grown up now, alright? Even if I didn't totally get it when I was younger, it probably only bugged me for like... a tiny bit.
I'm sure I got over it fast. Really fast!
Call it an adventure or call it running away. Either way, Karenina... I can't stay frozen in place forever. It's time I got moving.
A small boat carries two Gray Raven members back to the Balder. Soon after, the Vega blows her horn in parting and resumes her course.
In the dock bay, Karenina remains rooted in the salt wind, watching the sea until the Vega becomes a blur, then a fleck, then nothing at all against the gray horizon.
(Slowly walk over and stand beside her)
You came to wait for Lucia and Lee? It's pretty windy out here. Go wait in the crew quarters or up on the bridge. They'll come find you the second they're back.
Karenina cocks her head, wrestling her tone into something approaching casual indifference.
This way I can see them the moment they arrive.
What is this, school pickup? I'm not that sappy. I'm out of here!
She pivots with her chin raised, boot heels striking the deck in clean, sharp beats. Then she halts.
You know what, forget it. I'll... I'll wait with you. Just for a bit.
Without a word, you make room. Someone else slides into the gap at the same moment.
Boss, perfect timing. We need to lock down a few repeater parameters... The cable layer's waiting on this data. Also, Gray Raven Commandant! Huge honor. Can I get an autograph?
Captain, your frame's initial combat data couldn't upload because of the comms interference. We need to run a manual backup.
Gray Raven Commandant, I put together a tactical analysis based on your mission logs. Do you have a moment to look it over?
The two rookies from the Engineering Force press in from left and right, their data pads thrust so close they almost bump your nose.
Sure. You guys take care of the work first.

One step away from an unplanned swim, Karenina delivers a precise thwack to each of their heads and shoves those too-eager faces back. As they recoil, she spots the marine engineer strolling closer at an unhurried pace.
Let me guess. You need something too? Or are you also here for our BELOVED Gray Raven Commandant?
Uh... I don't mind waiting in line.
Though, Captain Karenina... looks like your surfboard brought something back from the sea. Something that doesn't belong on this ship.
The engineer's worried eyes guide every gaze toward the surfboard. It still hasn't reverted to its anchor form, seawater trailing in slow drips from its edges.
Nearby, where the light bleeds into shadow, a potted biosphere sits atop its metal stand, glowing dimly in the half-dark.
Feeling the weight of every gaze land on it at once, the potted plant's metal base sprouts several tiny articulated claws.
Skitter-skitter. Like a tiny animal busted mid-snack, the little potted plant flails its four mechanical claws and bolts across the deck in pure, undignified panic.
When you meet a stranger, always smile first.
With Lucia and Lee safely back aboard, the group gathers around the bridge's small tactical table.
Preliminary assessment shows no threat. A deep scan should take under two minutes.
Karenina cocks her head and hoists one of the tiny mechanical claws upside down, lifting it until it dangles right at eye level.
What the hell is this thing?
Placed back on the table, the odd little potted plant blooms a small yellow flower, aimed squarely at you.
Plant the stars, sail the seas, and always find your way. Your potted plant? No. Your precision navigator. Lear Mechanics, wherever you're headed.
The hell is it babbling about?
Advertisement. This is a mechanical potted plant. Maritime workers used them to grow whatever plants they liked. One of Lear Mechanics' more popular consumer products some thirty years back.
It runs its own ads? Smart hustle.
Well... the broadcast feature was likely added by the owner. The internals are simple enough, and it's loaded with expansion ports. Engineers back in the day loved customizing these things.
Which means... it wouldn't be hard to add something dangerous, either?
Lucia adjusts her stance by a fraction, ensuring that you, behind her, stay well within her guard.
Then let's just crack it open and find out! Move.
Wait, don't scroll past this classic! The Autumn Sale is live now.
Did it just... tell us to wait? Am I hearing that right? This thing's weirdly aware.
Arctic cod, the nutritionist your table deserves! Tender, flaky, and loaded with protein. Deliciously good for you!
Okay, those are all ad lines. But yeah. That's begging.
It's probably just trying to say that it's useful and harmless.
So like I said. Totally begging.
Deep scan's clean. No threats detected.
Lee sweeps his eyes across the room before his gaze comes to rest on you.
Its intelligence reads pretty high. But it shouldn't be an awakened machine.
Machines with this many expansion ports don't usually ship with advanced AI.
That's what's so weird about it!
Way too much strange crap floating around out here. Let me just crack it open and check.
Her talent for machinery is something close to divine. With nothing more than her fingertips and raw intuition, she homes in on the exact points where disassembly begins.
The girl presses her lips thin, a brief uncertainty flickering across her expression. She gives a small shake of her head and resumes the disassembly.
No one moves to stop Karenina. Everyone needs to know what secrets this strange little machine holds, and whether it carries some unknown danger.
Alright, let's see what we've got...
The instant she touches the potted plant's internal mechanism, something cold and mist-like wraps around her consciousness.
In a single violent jolt, the chill kicks her clean out of the glass cage.
A M.I.N.D. deviation alert shrieks through her systems.
A violent shudder climbs Karenina's spine and explodes at the top of her skull.
She finds herself in her consciousness space without knowing how she got there. A glass cage stands behind her, as real as anything.
She was trapped inside it, oblivious...
...until the chill from the potted plant's touch shocked her awake and kicked her loose.
Eyes fixed on the odd mechanical potted plant, Karenina remembers the sound from the fight: a low thud, as if something had dropped onto her surfboard.
You helped me? But why was I...
As the Engineering Force's vice-captain likes to say, Karenina's face might as well be a live feed of her thoughts. Nothing stays hidden there.
After she describes the strange anomalies her frame went through, she forces out a defense under the crushing weight of everyone's silent disapproval.
I thought it was just a calibration issue. Frame tuning, you know? Stuff I can handle on my own.
This doesn't look like a simple tuning issue.
Your eyes settle on the deep furrow of Lee's brow.
Karenina reported hearing whale calls twice. But the ship's monitoring equipment didn't register anything either time, and no Construct on site picked them up either.
We need to verify whether these whale calls actually exist before we can figure out what's happening to your frame. That's going to require support from the Science Council...
I can compile the data logs and send them up to Babylonia through Gray Raven's emergency channel.
Karenina stares at Lucia for a moment, then quietly turns her head away.

During the fight, this potted plant showed up, and your M.I.N.D. connection with Commandant came back online. Then just now, the moment you touched its internals, you broke free from that "glass mental cage"...
We can't say for sure whether it's dangerous. But keeping it somewhere we can monitor it would be the safest play. At least until we know if there's an actual causal link.
Then let's go with that. Thanks, Lee.
Good thing we've got you. Let's do that for now.
The whale calls Karenina described... None of our current equipment can detect them. To verify whether they're real, we'll need the Science Council's support.
Given the state of global communications right now, whether that report even gets through is... questionable at best.

During the fight, this potted plant showed up, and Karenina's M.I.N.D. connection with Commandant came back online. Then just now, the moment she touched its internals, she broke free from that "glass mental cage"...
We can't say for sure whether it's dangerous. But keeping it somewhere we can monitor it would be the safest play. At least until we know if there's an actual causal link.
I can compile the data logs and send them up to Babylonia through Gray Raven's emergency channel.
Karenina's gaze flickers to you, lingers on Lucia, then drifts aside, her head turning away.
It's what we do. You don't have to get all awkward about it.
Larsen examines the now-silent potted plant on the table, leaning in gradually until the internal structure is fully visible to the naked eye.
He indicates a flowing, cursive signature engraved on the inner metal face.
Cordelia. She was a friend of mine. Though maybe this next part will put you more at ease. She was also Dr. Kalon's first student in the Transatlantic Economic Community, and his favorite.
As though a hidden keyword has been tripped, the potted plant—silent and docile all this time—erupts with a bizarre, synthesized chitter of electronic noise.
Karenina catches her own name amid the electronic noise. Lee was right; this mechanical thing is far more intelligent than anyone would expect.
This appears to be the extent of its capabilities. It cannot string together another coherent word.
The little plant crackles with distorted static, then shifts. When it vocalizes again, you hear a young man's earnest and unpolished voice reciting something.
<color=#ffffffff><size=40>Sit on the other side of the light.</size></color>
<color=#ffffffff><size=40>the tide hums low in its throat.</size></color>
<color=#ffffffff><size=40>the banana split boat melts, sugar froth, a buttery sea.</size></color>

Sit on the other side of the light.
Blue ripples wash across the table.
Swaying, swaying,
the tide hums low in its throat.
Gray cotton candy swells
into the window's hollows.
Swaying, swaying,
the banana split boat melts, sugar froth, a buttery sea.
<color=#ffffffff><size=40>One, then two, the clown lets go.</size></color>
<color=#ffffffff><size=40>Down the spoon, ice cream balls slide into a hidden blue.</size></color>
<color=#ffffffff><size=40>Something sinks away, sugar froth, a sweet dream.</size></color>
<color=#ffffffff><size=40>Go sit on the other side of the light.</size></color>

One, then two, balloons rise.
One, then two, the clown lets go.
They scatter like wind-shredded notes.
Plop, plop.
Something sinks away, sugar froth, a sweet dream.
Go sit on the other side of the light.
A glint of tears rises in Larsen's eyes. He jerks his face aside in a hurry.
(That voice... is that the engineer? When he was young?)
God, that's awful. I really had no business writing poetry back then.
You can barely even call that a poem.
The bitter curve of his lips barely qualifies as a smile.
